title: Fractal Reality Principle
definition: The idea that larger systems can be represented or contained within smaller ones, implying that our universe might be a small part of a larger, more complex system.

difficulty_levels.beginner: The idea that a small amount of information can represent a larger, more complex system, like how an 18MB file can contain a digital ecosystem.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: The observation that a smaller system can embody a larger one, implying that our universe might be a smaller part of a larger, more complex system, as demonstrated by the ability of a digital ecosystem to fit within 18MB.
difficulty_levels.expert: The philosophical implication that larger systems can be contained within smaller ones, questioning the fundamental nature of reality and implying that our universe might be a small part of a larger, more complex system.

extra_fields.insight: The realization that our universe might be a small part of a larger, more complex system, as demonstrated by the ability of a digital ecosystem to fit within 18MB.
